title: The Ripple Counter
tagline: Two kinds of node, no code, and the lamps count in binary.
idea: Events can compute. A BooleanToggle is one bit of memory. A BooleanFilter's inputNegate says yes when its input says no, which is the moment a bit rolls over from 1 to 0. Chain them and you have built the counter inside every computer.

challenges.title: Count to fifteen
challenges.ask: Lamps 3 and 4 are dark. Wire them in so the counter reaches 15.
challenges.hint: Copy the pattern: Flip1.toggle goes to a new BooleanFilter, its inputNegate goes to a new BooleanToggle, and that toggle goes to Bit2's visible. Once more for Bit3.

challenges.title: Let a clock press the button
challenges.ask: Make it count by itself, once a second.
challenges.hint: A TimeSensor with loop on sends cycleTime (a time) every cycle. A BooleanTrigger turns a time into a yes. Send that yes to Flip0's set_boolean.

challenges.title: Count down
challenges.hint: Counting down borrows when a bit goes from 0 to 1. BooleanFilter has an output for that moment too: inputTrue. Use it in place of inputNegate.

script:
def counter():
    b = bg.Behaviour()
    press = b.add("TouchSensor", "Press", parent="Button", description="add one")
    flip0 = b.add("BooleanToggle", "Flip0")
    carry0 = b.add("BooleanFilter", "Carry0")
    flip1 = b.add("BooleanToggle", "Flip1")
    bit0 = b.target("Transform", "Bit0")
    bit1 = b.target("Transform", "Bit1")
    press.isActive >> flip0.set_boolean     # pressing sends yes; a BooleanToggle flips every time it hears yes
    flip0.toggle >> bit0.visible            # the flip shows or hides the first lamp
    flip0.toggle >> carry0.set_boolean      # the same flip also goes to a filter ...
    carry0.inputNegate >> flip1.set_boolean  # ... which says yes exactly when the lamp went OFF: that is the carry
    flip1.toggle >> bit1.visible
    return b
